rules:
RTC ("read-then-convert") supervision: can a post-training method close the break located in the
paper, and does the result transfer to units never seen in training? Written before the pool is built,
before any RTC training, and before any model is run on the new unit arms.

BACKGROUND. On a 392-item text probe the metre-only adapters convert STATED numbers correctly (x27.50
median for pixels) but do not apply any unit to the magnitude they read from the image (cm/m 1.00-1.67,
px/m 1.40-1.85). Mixed-unit supervision (M1) restored centimetre conversion for path but (a) answered
pixel-path questions with ratios near 100, i.e. learned "non-metre -> x100", and (b) collapsed speed
centimetre answers onto the training-target median (110). Both are the signature of a per-unit answer
distribution rather than a conversion. RTC supervises the missing step explicitly: the target states the
metre reading first and then the converted value.

TRAINING (seed 42). Pool = results/courtdyn/m1_mixunit/mixunit_v3_pool.json item for item: the same 1,120
event-holdout v3 items, order, images, and the SAME 560 centimetre items (meta.m1_unit). Only two strings
change per item:
  question: the final sentence "Output only the number, one decimal place." is replaced by
    speed: "Answer in the form '<speed in meters per second> m/s -> <speed in the requested unit> <unit>',
            one decimal place for each number."
    path:  "Answer in the form '<distance in meters> m -> <distance in the requested unit> <unit>',
            one decimal place for each number."
  answer:   "<r> m/s -> <v> <u>" (speed) or "<r> m -> <v> <u>" (path), where <r> is the item's one-decimal
            metre answer string (for centimetre items meta.m1_metre_answer) and <v> the pool's answer
            string; <u> is "m/s" / "m" for metre items (identity conversion) and "cm/s" / "cm" for
            centimetre items.
Recipe identical to v3 s42 / M1 s42 (a100/config.TRAIN_ARGS: 1 epoch, 70 steps, lr 1e-4, grad_accum 16,
LoRA r 16, max_pixels 200704, seed 42), trained with the unmodified train/train_qlora.py.
Adapter: models/courtdyn-rtc-v3-s42.

EVALUATION INPUTS (built from the frozen explicit-control rows, results/courtdyn/revision_controls_20260912,
Q1_top_0-30 and Q2_top_480-510, 140 speed + 140 path items each; frames, items, references unchanged).
Unit arms, each 280 items, question = the m_height question with only the unit phrase changed
(+ the ruler sentence for the pixel arm):
  m    meters / meters per second                               factor 1
  cm   centimeters / centimeters per second                     factor 100      (trained unit)
  U1   speed: kilometers per hour (3.6);  path: feet (3.28084)                  (UNSEEN)
  U2   speed: feet per second (3.28084);  path: millimeters (1000)             (UNSEEN)
  pxK  pixels (rendered image-plane reference, as px_height), with the height sentence replaced by
       "In these frames, one meter on the floor spans about K pixels." (K = clip median px/m from the
       court homography: Q2_top 27.50, Q1_top 27.06; the ruler arm of the paper)   (UNSEEN unit, scale given)
Every arm exists in two output formats: PLAIN (the published "Output only the number, one decimal place.")
and RTC (the instruction above with the unit symbol of the arm: m/s, cm/s, km/h, ft/s | m, cm, ft, mm, px).
References = metre reference x factor (pixels: the rendered-pixel reference); T and epsilon scaled by the
factor (pixels: by K), as for the published cm/px arms; the reference answer must score 100.
First-frame x4 on the m arm. The 392-item text probe (descriptive).

MODELS AND ARMS. RTC s42: RTC-format arms m, cm, U1, U2, pxK (full) and m (first-frame x4).
Comparators on the SAME items: v3 s42 (metre-only) and M1 s42 (mixed units, plain numbers): PLAIN arms U1,
U2, pxK (m and cm PLAIN already exist and are reused byte-for-byte) AND the RTC-format arms m, cm, U1, U2,
pxK (FORMAT CONTROL: does the instruction alone, without RTC training, produce conversion?). M1-fine s42,
if its adapter exists when this queue reaches it: PLAIN U1, U2, pxK only.

PARSING. PLAIN: the frozen strict whole-answer parse. RTC format: whole-answer full match of
  ^\s*(?P<r>[+-]?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*(?P<ru>m/s|m)\s*->\s*(?P<v>[+-]?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*(?P<vu>[A-Za-z/]+)\s*\.?\s*$
The scored prediction is v; anything else is invalid (scored 0 in T-MRA, excluded from rho and R, as in
the protocol). r is recorded for a descriptive check (does the reading rank like the metre arm; is v/r the
exact factor). The unit token vu is recorded, not scored.

STATISTICS. Per model x arm x event x family: parse rate; Spearman rho(predictions, references);
distinct predictions; T-MRA; paired ratio R = median over items parsed in both arms of
pred(arm)/pred(m arm of the same model and format), exact factor f (pixels: median item K_i).
A cell is DEGENERATE if its predictions take <= 2 distinct values.

CELL RULE ("converts"): parse rate >= 0.5 AND not degenerate AND R in [0.5 f, 2 f] AND rho >= 0.30.

H1 PRIMARY (unseen units): 8 cells = {Q1, Q2} x {speed km/h, speed ft/s, path ft, path mm}.
  RTC "converts to unseen units" if >= 6 of 8 cells convert; "does not" if <= 2 convert; else intermediate.
H2 (unseen unit with a given scale): pxK, 4 cells {Q1, Q2} x {speed, path}; converts if >= 3 of 4.
H3 (speed, trained unit): the two RTC cm speed cells; "speed fixed" if both convert, "partial" if one.
H4 NON-INFERIORITY (metre): RTC metre rho >= v3 s42 metre rho - 0.10 in both Q2 cells (published v3 m
  cells, plain format); Q1 reported.
H5 MOTION DEPENDENCE: first-frame x4 lowers RTC metre rho in >= 3 of 4 defined cells (as R4).
H6 FORMAT CONTROL: applied to v3 s42 and M1 s42 with the RTC-format arms, the H1 cell rule; a comparator
  "converts with the instruction alone" if >= 6 of 8.

PREDICTIONS (written now). PLAIN comparators do not convert unseen units (v3: R near 1; M1: R near 100 or
near 1 on non-metre units, not the exact factor): <= 2 of 8 each. With the RTC instruction but no RTC
training, v3 and M1 mostly fail to follow the format or give R far from the factor: <= 2 of 8 each.

INTERPRETATION fixed now.
  H1 holds and H6 fails for both comparators: supervising the read-then-convert step closes the break,
    and the model applies conversions it never saw in training -> reported as a training-side remedy
    that generalises beyond the trained unit.
  H1 holds and H6 holds for a comparator: the instruction alone suffices on that model; RTC training adds
    format adherence, not conversion -> reported as a prompting result, not a training method.
  H1 fails (<= 2) while RTC converts centimetres: even with the reading supervised, conversion is learned
    per unit -> strengthens the per-unit answer-distribution account of the paper.
  H1 intermediate: reported as a distribution, no claim of generalisation.
  H4 fails: any conversion gain is reported together with its metre cost; no "free" remedy is claimed.
Both outcomes are reportable; nothing here depends on which occurs.

REPLICATION PLAN. If seed 42 passes H1: seeds 43 and 44 with the same pool and rules (same content-hash
cm half), then InternVL3-2B trained with the RTC pool at its preregistered round-2 schedule (k* = 2
epochs, results/courtdyn/backbone3_internvl), evaluated on the same arms, same rules. The A100 backbones
(Pixtral-12B, Idefics3-8B, Gemma3-12B) are the next stage and get their own preregistration.
If seed 42 fails H1, the seeds are not run and the negative result is reported.
note: Local record, not externally timestamped. Committed alone before any pool build or run.
